title: OSPF Multi-Area: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Picture a company with a headquarters and several branches. Every branch talks to the others through HQ. That's multi area O S P F.

scenes.heading: HQ and branches
scenes.narration: Area zero is headquarters. Every other area, a branch, must connect straight to area zero. The router between a branch and HQ is the A B R. The A B R passes summaries using type three L S As. A router joining an outside network is an A S B R, with type five.

scenes.heading: Stub areas
scenes.narration: Branches can ask for less detail. A stub blocks type five, and a totally stubby area blocks types three, four and five. A stub keeps inter area routes, but totally stubby just gets a default. Both exist to shrink the routing table.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. An A B R needs at least one interface in area zero. Type three only carries the prefix and metric. A stub area blocks only type five.

items.wrong: An ABR needs two non-backbone areas
Stub blocks all external and inter-area
